title: BMO Demonstrates Quantum Utility in Game-Theoretic Machine Learning Feature Selection on IBM Nighthawk r2 - Quantum Computing Report
gist: BMO, with Democritus University of Thrace and IBM, ran a quantum game-theoretic (Proxy Quantum Games) feature-selection workflow on IBM processors including Nighthawk r2, claiming classical-comparable quality with one to two orders of magnitude fewer samples. Key hardware and runtime details are unpublished and BMO calls it early-stage.

insights.claim: BMO, Democritus University of Thrace and IBM demonstrated a quantum machine learning feature-selection workflow on IBM superconducting processors, including the IBM Quantum Nighthawk r2 system, for financial datasets used in client modeling, risk assessment and personalization.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Banks are moving quantum pilots onto IBM's newest hardware, supporting IBM's enterprise quantum narrative.

insights.claim: BMO reports its quantum ranking approach matched classical baselines on feature-selection quality while needing one to two orders of magnitude fewer algorithmic samples.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A sample-efficiency claim rather than a quality gain; the commercial edge depends on unpublished runtime and cost data.

insights.claim: BMO has not published qubit counts, circuit depths, or wall-clock runtime comparisons for its quantum feature-selection result, so the claimed quantum utility cannot yet be independently assessed.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Treat 'quantum utility' headlines from finance pilots with skepticism until benchmarks are disclosed.

insights.claim: The Proxy Quantum Games framework models each candidate dataset variable as a player in a quantum strategic game, with higher payoff for variables aligned to the target outcome and lower payoff for uninformative or redundant ones.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A reusable approach for casting ML preprocessing as a quantum game; watch for adoption beyond BMO.
